prototype: Opt-in composer search restarted each trial from original separations and coordinates, retained logs and counts, used explicit negative-cycle choice prefixes, and bounded trials/frontier/coupled passes to 16 each. Ordinary first-choice repair was tried first; both axes, hard terms and physical separations were checked before accepting a branch.

carrier_screen.compact_and_noncompact: Each executed branch trial 1 only: X succeeded, Y succeeded after flips, then X failed with a negative cycle. Frontier was empty; no additional eligible flip choice was available along the executed prefix.

finding: Branching over eligible edges of the detected negative cycles does not rescue this carrier case: the observed prefix contains no alternative eligible choices. This is a narrower limitation than a global infeasibility proof. The original composition stage fixes all interior blocks except hard-term participants also present in compose.wired_participants; fixed usb_jtag/FMC and SoM escape regions constrain hdmi_rx_term.
decision: Removed all six prototype-file diffs with apply_patch, verified exact HEAD restoration, rebuilt profiler and floorplan regression binaries. The previously committed explicit axis-choice API remains; no ineffective composer branch loop or extra profiler option retained.
next_direction: Review movement eligibility and bounded blocker displacement at the composition boundary. Do not infer permission to move a fixed or hardware-constrained block merely from its presence in a failed cycle. Investigate a permitted neighbour or earlier placement choice rather than adding more identical cycle retries.
limitations: No smaller board accepted, source/design gate waived, or production performance improvement claimed.
One motivating carrier case; broader applicability of alternative cycle choices remains unproven.
Existing qualified layouts and unrelated untracked evidence preserved.
